title: Software development and rules stability: Prototype racing in 2030
gist: Sportscar racing is growing, with IMSA's audience up over a third domestically last year, but manufacturer retrenchment (Porsche, Alpine, Acura) and Middle East disruption threaten the grid. Stakeholders including IMSA's John Doonan and Porsche's Urs Kuratle favor merging the LMDh and Hypercar rulesets into one from 2030, with IMSA's LMDh evolution likely to win.

insights.claim: IMSA's audience grew by more than a third domestically and almost a quarter internationally last year, helped by multi-hour, multi-class racing suiting streaming and second screens.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Rising viewership supports sponsor and OEM marketing value of endurance racing.

insights.claim: Open paddocks and grid walks that draw huge crowds make IMSA fan access nearly unmatched, and IMSA President John Doonan says the series is just scratching the surface.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Fan access is a differentiator for sponsor activation and ticket demand.
insights.quote: “I think we’re just scratching the surface,”

insights.claim: Porsche cut its factory prototype program in half last year, parking its two WEC cars and keeping two in IMSA, blamed mostly on an EV transition that has not come and Trump's tariffs hitting US profits.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Auto OEM motorsport budgets track economic and tariff pressure, so cuts are an indicator of OEM financial stress.

insights.claim: Alpine is retiring from the WEC at the end of the year, a Geely rescue is now unlikely, and Acura is ending its IMSA GTP program to focus on IndyCar, meaning no Honda presence at Le Mans in the near future.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Program exits shrink the top-class grid and signal reduced marketing spend at Honda and Renault's Alpine.
insights.locator: But Porsche is not the only one

insights.claim: The war in the Middle East has disrupted both the World Endurance Championship and a new Asian Le Mans series, and the top level depends on manufacturer largesse that usually vanishes with worsening economic outlooks.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Geopolitical shocks and downturns hit discretionary motorsport spend first.

insights.claim: Genesis entered the WEC this year and Ford and McLaren will join WEC next year, filling space left by departing programs.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: New entrants partly offset exits, making the trajectory still positive.
insights.locator: Then again, the end of those other programs

insights.claim: All three factory efforts chose IMSA's LMDh regulations over Le Mans' Hypercar rules, which allow more freedom such as all-wheel-drive hybrid systems and bespoke batteries but cost more.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: OEMs are voting with budgets for cost-controlled, spec-component racing.
insights.locator: One reg to rule them all?

insights.claim: Most stakeholders agree two rulesets are daft and want one category from 2030 when the current rulesets expire.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: A single global prototype category would lower OEM costs and could attract more manufacturers.
insights.locator: The good news is that most stakeholders

insights.claim: Urs Kuratle, head of Porsche's prototype program, said it would have been clever to use one ruleset from the beginning, but the two rulesets worked and enabled the sports car renaissance.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Porsche supports consolidation, consistent with cost containment.
insights.quote: If you would ask, it would have been clever to do it with one rule set from just beginning, the answer would also be yes. But it worked
insights.locator: “The way to go forward is to have one category.

insights.claim: Doonan expects the next regulations to be an evolution of LMDh and says rules stability is critical so automakers and sponsors like Michelin and Motul can come to market when headwinds arrive.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: IMSA's rules are the likely template, favoring OEMs already invested in LMDh.
insights.locator: What does this sport look like in five years?

insights.claim: Porsche's T-hybrid engine and electric turbocharger descend directly from the 919 Hybrid race car, but direct technology transfer is less common now and software is the more likely transfer channel.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Racing relevance for OEMs is shifting from hardware to software and data.
insights.locator: One reason some of us love prototype racing

insights.claim: IMSA Labs offers race data to researchers and developers to build software, business solutions, AI and predictive analysis, and OEMs say hybrid-system strategy learnings feed road car development.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Data licensing and OEM development value could support the economic case for the series.
insights.locator: Now IMSA Labs has opened up
